exposure: mode of delivery (vaginal delivery, elective cesarean section)
Mode of delivery: vaginal vs elective caesarean section
outcome: Admission to neonatal intensive care unit (NICU)
cohort: 1327 singleton term breech fetuses delivered vaginally or by elective caesarean section from January 2012 to October 2014
finding: Although vaginal breech delivery was associated with lower Apgar scores and a higher incidence of fetal trauma, overall rates of these events were low, and admission to the NICU and maternal outcomes were similar between vaginal and elective caesarean delivery.
mod_finding: Vaginal breech delivery was associated with lower Apgar scores and higher incidence of fetal trauma compared to elective caesarean section, but both delivery routes seem equally valid, neither posing high maternal or neonatal complications' incidence.
